name: Surprise — The Pleasure of the Unexpected
summary: Variety keeps sensation exciting—65–76% of women prefer non-repetitive stimulation at some stage of arousal. Surprise means alternating between different pleasurable variations to keep the body guessing, not throwing in unrelated distractions.
detailed_description: OMGYES describes two approaches to surprise: constant surprise (make every motion different from the last) and set surprise (repeat a motion a few times to build, then switch before it gets predictable). Surprise is about varied pleasurable moves, not random 'zingers.' An important exception: once the approach begins and an orgasm is building, many prefer to drop the surprise and stay consistent with one motion.
stepwise_structure: 1. Start from a move that already works for the receiver.
2. Choose an approach: constant surprise (vary every repetition) or set surprise (build then switch).
3. Vary by shape, location, and/or speed/rhythm—keep changes pleasurable, not jarring.
4. Use a signal so you know when the receiver is getting close.
5. When the orgasm starts building (the approach), drop the surprise and hold one consistent motion.
safety_notes: Surprise means alternating pleasurable variations, not unrelated or distracting touches mid-flow.
Stop varying and stay consistent once orgasm is building unless told otherwise.
Adults in consensual contexts only; not a substitute for professional care.

practical_tips.signal_system: Agree on a cue (e.g. 'getting close!') so the giver knows when to stop switching and stay consistent.
practical_tips.timing_balance: More intense motions work best in short bursts; gentler or indirect moves can repeat longer without feeling repetitive.
practical_tips.not_random_zingers: Surprise is alternating pleasurable variations, not introducing unrelated distractions mid-flow.

meta.approach_exception: Once orgasm starts building, many prefer one consistent motion over continued surprise.
